transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Um, hi. Well... I guess I'm just here because I've been having this constant restless feeling. It's a bit hard to explain, but I just feel kind of wound too tight, I suppose. Like I can't fully settle down. Even when I'm supposed to be sitting calmly—like in a planning meeting for work, or... or even just trying to paint or do yoga. I just can't seem to settle.
How long have you been experiencing this restless, wound-up feeling—days, weeks, or has it been going on for years, even since childhood?

Um... well, I suppose it's been noticeably harder to manage for a while now. Maybe about two years and... two months, give or take. It just sort of escalated when... well, when some conflicts with my in-laws started taking over a lot of our evenings. I'd rather not get into all the family drama, but... yeah, a little over two years.
Besides feeling restless, have you noticed any physical changes like unexplained weight loss, a racing heart, excessive sweating, or feeling unusually hot even when others are comfortable?
Um... no. Not really. I haven't lost any weight, and... I don't think my heart races or anything like that. It's really just the... the wound-up feeling I mentioned.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a number of different things—like work, health, or family—and having a hard time controlling or stopping that worry once it starts?
Um... no, not really. I don't think I worry any more than anyone else does. I don't really dwell on things like that... it's just that physical feeling I mentioned.

Thinking back to when you were a child or teenager, did you notice similar feelings of restlessness, difficulty sitting still, or trouble focusing back then, or is this something that only started as an adult?

Um... well... I suppose it's not entirely new. I mean, when I was younger, I guess I had some trouble with that sort of thing. 

Like... in elementary school, my parents would get notes from the teachers. I guess I had a hard time staying in my chair. And... well, they said I talked over the other kids a lot. I'd just sort of blurt things out before the teacher was even done asking the question. But... that was a long time ago.

After childhood, did you continue to notice ongoing difficulties with restlessness, staying focused, or impulsivity throughout your teenage years and into adulthood, or did those symptoms mostly go away until recently?

Um... I suppose it never completely went away. I just... dealt with it, mostly. But... it's been noticeably harder to manage lately. For about... maybe two years and two months now. Just... since we started having some conflicts with my in-laws. It ends up taking over a lot of our evenings, and... well, it's just been harder since that started.
Aside from what's happening at home with your in-laws, have you also noticed these restless or distractible feelings causing problems for you at work or in other areas of your life?

Um... I suppose so. At work... well, I've had a few purchase orders that needed to be corrected. My planning coordinator has started doing extra reviews on my stuff lately. It's... well, it is what it is. 

And I guess at home... family dinners can get a little tense. They... well, people say they feel like I talk over them. So... yeah. I guess it causes some problems.
